GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: One-step rollback, not a version vault. The research session of 2026-10-28 surveyed how others handle a bad update: JetBrains Toolbox "keeps a previously installed version of each tool — this is by design to enable instant rollback. You can delete previous versions to save space"; Windows offers "Go back" for ~10 days after an upgrade and then deletes Windows.old; TestFlight exposes "View Previous Builds"; Adobe Creative Cloud allows installing previous versions (two majors deep for individuals); Discord on Windows accidentally allows rollback because Squirrel leaves the two latest version folders on disk, but its updater immediately re-offers the update — the cautionary example; Chrome's enterprise rollback documents the data price (user data written by the newer version is lost without Sync), which is why a preferences snapshot is part of this design rather than an afterthought. Mass-market apps without rollback (VS Code, Zoom) bet on their crash rate; a small team with a 24-hour auto-check fleet and no staging ring should not. Depth of exactly one: the realistic incident is "the version I just took is bad", one step back restores yesterday's known-good state, and one staged copy on macOS (one bundle in the data root — ≈ 32 MB on disk at v2.8.2, measured from the release tarball, with a transient ≈ 64 MB peak during staging — outside the shipped bundle) is the whole footprint cost. Fail-closed prepare: an update applied without a restorable snapshot is strictly worse than a delayed update; and the restore re-verifies what it is about to swap, because a rollback that bricks the last known-good state is worse than no rollback. Skip-the-departed-version reuses the shipped exact-match skip semantics (Sparkle's "Skip This Version" pattern), so a fixed newer release still reaches the user. The terminal path exists because every in-app surface dies with the UI; the owner explicitly requested it (owner, 2026-10-28, translated: "we need a terminal CLI command for the case when the UI crashes — write about it in the guides and the FAQ"; also cited in the spec Constraints).

Alternatives.Alternative: Version vault (keep N previous versions, JetBrains-style selectable list): rejected — multiplies data-root footprint and UI surface for a case (multi-step back) that almost never occurs; one step covers the incident class.

Download-previous-on-demand on macOS as well (fetch the old DMG at restore time, like Windows): rejected for v1 — DMG mount-and-copy is more new code than restoring an already-staged bundle copy, and it makes crash recovery depend on network access on the platform where offline restore is otherwise free.

Server-driven fleet rollback (feed answers with a lower version plus a custom version_comparator so every client downgrades): rejected — moving the whole fleet backward at once is a bigger blast radius than the disease, and it needs feed-side infrastructure this repo does not run; recorded as a future change if ever needed.

Automatic crash-loop detection with auto-rollback: rejected for v1 — heuristics on "crashes at boot" risk false positives (a machine with a broken GPU driver would silently pin itself to an old version and stop receiving fixes).

Keeping the old setup.exe on disk on Windows at update time: rejected — doubles Windows footprint for a file that is already published and signature-covered on GitHub Releases; on-demand fetch verified with the updater's own minisign anchor keeps the disk cost at one small manifest.

Cheapest MVP (a "Download previous version" link in Help plus the existing skip flag, no restore code): rejected by the owner's direction — the crash case has no working UI to click a link in, which is exactly why the terminal command is in scope.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Exact id of the new governed module and verification anchor (next free M-0NN / V-M-0NN) — confirmed by the plan before any graph write.
Exact installed executable path on Windows for the guide commands (NSIS per-user vs per-machine layout) — pinned against the shipped installer at plan time.
Prompt copy details for the CLI y/N confirmation and the exact machine-readable output line format — fixed at plan time together with the verification markers.

The concrete mechanism of the pre-boot live-instance probe (reusing the single-instance plugin's channel vs a dedicated lock file) — chosen at plan time; the spec pins only the behavior (delegate to the running app, never a headless swap under it).

Scenarios.Scenario: Crash recovery (the reason this change exists): 2.9.1 ships, the notice greets the user on the next launch, Update installs it — and the new version crashes at boot. The user opens Terminal, runs the command from the FAQ, answers y, and 2.9.0 is back with its settings and without a re-offer of 2.9.1. When 2.9.2 ships with the fix, the notice appears and updating is one click — with a fresh rollback snapshot of 2.9.0 taken first.
Healthy regret: 2.9.0 runs fine but the user dislikes it. Help → "Roll Back to Mark 2.8.2…", confirmation explains the settings revert, restore, done.

Windows polygon: same regret on Windows; Mark fetches the 2.8.2 setup.exe from the v2.8.2 release, verifies its minisignature from that release's latest.json against the app-pinned updater pubkey, runs it passively, relaunches.

C-1.Name: Headless crash recovery
C-1.Situation: UI-crash recovery, the core case: the newly updated version crashes at boot; no Mark window can open; the user runs the binary by full path with --rollback from a terminal (the exact command documented in guide/faq.md).
C-1.Expected: The restore runs headless (macOS flow; Windows follows the per-platform ordering in R-3): TTY y/N confirmation (non-interactive runs require --yes and decline without it, exit 5); staged previous bundle is re-verified against its recorded digest, then swapped over the current bundle path; preferences snapshot restored atomically; skippedUpdateVersion set to the departed version; staging directory deleted; app relaunches as the previous version; exit code 0; every step emits its structured marker ([Rollback][*][BLOCK_*]) to the terminal transcript.

C-2.Name: Second launch while a healthy instance runs
C-2.Situation: A second launch of mark --rollback while a healthy instance is running. The single-instance plugin registers only during app init, so the pre-boot --rollback handler itself must detect the live instance; manifest validity is resolved locally first (an invalid set reports exit 7 before any probe).
C-2.Expected: No headless swap under a running app and no second process: the pre-boot handler probes for a live instance; a live instance answers, the handler delegates by asking the running instance to open the in-app rollback confirmation dialog (R-4) and exits 0 with a machine-readable line distinguishing delegation from restore; cancelling the dialog changes nothing; a repeated invocation while the dialog is already open focuses the existing dialog instead of stacking another.

C-3.Name: No snapshot available
C-3.Situation: No valid rollback set exists: the user updated from a pre-feature version (that hop was never snapshotted), or the set was cleared by an earlier restore.
C-3.Expected: The Help menu shows no rollback item; the CLI prints that no snapshot exists together with the address of the release-history page for a manual download, and exits 7; no partial writes, no network access.

C-4.Name: Snapshot failure at update time
C-4.Situation: Snapshot preparation fails at update time (disk full, data root unwritable, digest of the staged copy mismatches on readback).
C-4.Expected: Fail-closed: downloadAndInstall is never invoked; the user-visible flow reports that the update was cancelled because a rollback snapshot could not be prepared; the running version is untouched; no half-valid manifest or staging directory remains (atomic temp-sibling staging with cleanup on error; a stale temp sibling from an earlier interrupted run is removed at this point too); if the failure happens later — a download or install that fails after a successful prepare — the previous live set is untouched (promotion happens only after success), so the older escape hatch survives.

C-5.Name: Settings changed after updating
C-5.Situation: The user changed settings after updating (new prefs keys written by the newer version) and then rolls back.
C-5.Expected: Both confirmation surfaces (dialog and CLI) warn that settings return to the pre-update snapshot; the restore writes the snapshot over the canonical preferences file; the previous version boots with known-good settings; the departed preferences file is not preserved.

C-6.Name: App moved to a non-default location
C-6.Situation: The app was moved to a non-default location between the update and the rollback (e.g. /Applications to ~/Apps on macOS), or the bundle path is unwritable.
C-6.Expected: Restore targets the bundle path the app actually runs from (current executable ancestry), never a hardcoded /Applications; the departed bundle goes to Trash so the user can inspect it; an unwritable bundle path fails closed with exit 6 and a clear message (no privileged helpers, never a half-swap); a Trash failure after a successful swap is logged and non-blocking; on Windows the installer's own logic decides the location.

C-7.Name: Windows verification failure
C-7.Situation: Windows restore: the downloaded installer's minisignature does not verify against the app-pinned updater pubkey (signature taken from that release's latest.json asset), or the download fails mid-transfer, or the release predates the Windows asset (WINDOWS_RELEASE off).
C-7.Expected: The installer is never executed; the failure is reported with exit code 4; the rollback set stays intact; a retry is possible; when the asset simply does not exist for that release, the message points to the release-history page for a manual download; nothing outside the staging area is written; the CLI has already exited 0 with the outcome pending at spawn time — an installer run that fails after verification keeps the set and is detected by the departed version at its next launch, which re-offers an idempotent retry (a failed Windows attempt has already restored the pre-update preferences snapshot; the retry re-restores the same snapshot, and the confirmation consented to that revert).

C-8.Name: App-store build exposes nothing
C-8.Situation: App-store build (MAS / TestFlight): any rollback surface.
C-8.Expected: None: no menu item, no manifest writes, no restore code path reachable; mark --rollback prints the "Updates are managed by the App Store" message (same voice as mt_updater_check) and exits 3; the M-048 capability map reports no rollback capability to the renderer.

C-9.Name: Fixed newer release after rollback
C-9.Situation: Rollback, then a fixed newer release ships (2.9.1 skipped by rollback; 2.9.2 released).
C-9.Expected: The notice for 2.9.2 appears normally (skip is exact-version by the existing autoUpdates.js semantics); updating to 2.9.2 snapshots 2.9.0 first, refreshing the rollback set and cleaning the old staging; the cycle continues.

C-10.Name: Repeated rollback attempt
C-10.Situation: Repeated rollback attempt with no fresh update in between (rollback of a rollback).
C-10.Expected: Not offered: the manifest was cleared by the successful restore, so the menu item is absent and the CLI behaves as the no-snapshot case (C-3, exit 7); moving forward again happens only through the normal update flow.

C-11.Name: Prefs restore failure after bundle swap
C-11.Situation: Preferences restore fails after the bundle swap already succeeded (macOS).
C-11.Expected: The restore still completes and relaunches the previous version: the bundle is the load-bearing step; the preferences step failure is logged with its marker and the current (newer-version) preferences file is left in place; the old version's tolerance of unknown newer keys (m005_prefs never errors on unknown keys) is covered by a regression test.

C-12.Name: Corrupted or tampered rollback set
C-12.Situation: After a successful prepare, the manifest or the staged bundle is corrupted on disk, edited by hand, or written by an older buggy run (digest mismatch, unknown schema, platform mismatch, staged path escaping the data root, stored version disagreeing with the deterministic derivation).
C-12.Expected: Fail closed as "no snapshot": an invalid manifest hides the menu item and the CLI exits 7 with no network access; a digest mismatch discovered at restore time aborts before any swap with the current state untouched (exit 6); injected path or URL material in the manifest is rejected before any fetch; nothing is ever half-applied.

C-13.Name: Failed update attempt
C-13.Situation: Prepare succeeds (fresh snapshot staged), but the download or the install fails — the user is still on the current version, e.g. still on a broken 2.9.1 whose escape attempt to 2.9.2 just failed.
C-13.Expected: The previous live set is untouched and still valid (promotion to the live set happens only after the update is applied), so the older escape hatch survives; no self-rollback surface appears (a manifest whose previous version equals the running version is invalid by definition and can never surface — R-1 promotes only after success, R-3 validity rejects it defensively); retrying the update re-runs prepare; on Windows a failed installer run keeps the set and the departed version re-offers the retry at next launch.

Review.Findings: Round 1, two independent fresh agents covering four corners (A: Correctness and Contracts + Performance and Footprint; B: Security and Privacy + UX and Docs). Verdict: changes-requested — 0 blocking, 4 important, 8 notes; all fixed in the same edit pass. (F1 IMPORTANT) R-5/C-2 described single-instance forwarding that cannot fire: the plugin registers during app init, after all pre-boot main() code — replaced with a pre-boot live-instance probe that delegates to the running app's dialog. (F2 IMPORTANT) Windows restore silently depended on the WINDOWS_RELEASE repo variable gating the artifact set — precondition now stated in R-2 and Assumptions, with the release-history fallback documented. (S-1 IMPORTANT) "signed NSIS installer" was false (the pipeline has no Authenticode) and SHA-256-vs-release-assets.sha256 was same-channel only — restore now verifies the installer's minisignature from the release's latest.json against the app-pinned updater pubkey, the same anchor as every update. (S-2 IMPORTANT) staged-bundle integrity and manifest validity were unspecified at restore time — manifest now records SHA-256 digests, restore re-verifies before any swap, validity is strict and invalid = no-snapshot, new corner C-12. Notes also applied: exit code 2 left to clap usage errors (no-snapshot renumbered to 7); unverifiable "hotfix-lane" motivation replaced with the citable FIX-017/FIX-018 incident (docs/release-trains/2.7.x-next.md:72); stale-temp-sibling cleanup pinned; transient 2x staging peak quantified; FAQ title made question-form per the file's convention; Docs criterion extended with the first-hop caveat and the adjust-the-path hint; CLI output declared English-only; non-interactive runs require --yes; dialog stacking prevented; unwritable-bundle and Trash-failure policies written; injected-path-material rejection pinned by test.

Round 2, two fresh independent agents, same four corners. Verdict: changes-requested — 0 blocking, 2 important, 7 notes; all fixed in the same edit pass. (A1 IMPORTANT) R-2 named a SHA-256 corruption guard with no digest source inside the two-fetch bound — clause removed; the pinned-anchor minisign check covers integrity and authenticity. (B1 IMPORTANT) the CLI y/N prompt carried none of the dialog's mandatory disclosures — R-5 and the CLI criterion now require the prompt to print the target version, the settings revert and the skip of the departed version, with only exact wording deferred. Notes also applied: budget wording corrected (Phase-B target + the CI-enforced 20 MB Windows installer gate, "within" not "unchanged"); VerificationIntent suite paths switched to real files (tests/renderer/commands/updater.test.js, tests/renderer/menu-bridge.test.js); "app-store builds never write a rollback manifest" pinned in the Snapshot criterion; signing-key rotation honesty added to R-2 (pre-rotation restores exit 4 with the release-history fallback); fetched-feed version field cross-checked against the manifest before its signature entry is used; executed-installer byte identity (re-digest or verified-handle spawn immediately before execution) pinned; delegation edge cases defined (validity resolved before the probe, exit 7 wins; successful delegation is exit 0 distinguished by its machine-readable line).

Round 3, two fresh independent agents. Security/Privacy and UX/Docs corner: clean. Correctness corner: 0 blocking, 1 important, 3 notes; all fixed in the same edit pass. (A1 IMPORTANT) R-3 told Windows to exit for the installer and "then" restore preferences and relaunch — unsatisfiable after exit and contradicting the binding fail-closed ordering; ordering is now per-platform (macOS: swap before prefs+skip writes; Windows: prefs+skip writes before the installer spawn, the manifest finalized only after confirmed success by the restored version at next launch, and a failed installer run leaves the set recoverable), and Constraints item 3 matches. Notes also applied: a live-but-broken instance that cannot show the dialog no longer strands the CLI path (acknowledgment timeout, treated as absent; FAQ says quit and rerun); the crash-recovery scenario and rationale no longer say "auto-installs" (Mark auto-checks, the user clicks); footprint reads as the 30 MB budget with ≈ 11 MB measured, not ≈ 30 MB actual; macOS self-consistent digests recorded as the consciously accepted bound; renderer-exposed restore command re-validates in Rust with the dialog as the only intended entry; "clear the manifest/set" unified to "delete the entire staging directory"; menu label scoped to the existing English m009 menu-string convention (ten locales cover dialog and notices).

Round 4, two fresh independent agents. Verdict: changes-requested — 0 blocking, 3 important, 3 notes; all fixed in the same edit pass. (A1 IMPORTANT) the failed-update-attempt state was unhandled: R-1 replaced the live set at prepare time, so a failed download destroyed the escape hatch and offered a nonsensical self-rollback — R-1 now promotes the fresh snapshot to the live set only after the update is applied (failed attempts leave the previous set untouched), R-3 validity rejects a manifest equal to the running version defensively, and new corner C-13 pins the state. (B1 IMPORTANT) "treated as absent after timeout" contradicted the no-swap-under-a-live-instance rule — a broken live instance now makes the command decline with exit 6 and quit-first instructions; never a swap under a live instance. (B2 IMPORTANT) the Windows "installer run fails (exit 6)" cell was unreachable (the CLI exits before the installer outcome exists) — Windows exit semantics pinned: exit 0 at spawn with the outcome pending, failure detected by the departed version at next launch, which keeps the set and re-offers an idempotent retry. Notes also applied: the FAQ enumeration and Docs criterion now include the quit-Mark-first advice and the Windows exit-0-pending meaning; a failed Windows attempt's already-reverted preferences and the idempotent retry are stated in C-7.

Round 5, two fresh independent agents. VERDICT: clean on both corners (0 blocking, 0 important; 7 notes). First clean pass of the required two consecutive. Notes applied between passes: the equals-running-version rejection added to the Validity criterion's strictness list; the CLI criterion's exit-0 parenthetical now names the Windows installer-spawned-pending case; the Rationale's footprint figure updated to the live v2.8.2 measurement (≈ 14 MB; 11 MB was the B1.5 gate figure); the accepted same-user bound extended to the Windows staging directory and version-only manifest; the in-app Windows path quiesces pending preference writes before the restore writes (sequencing fixed at plan time); the R-7/Docs enumeration gains the release-history manual-download fallback for exits 4 and 7; AffectedAreas names the generate_handler! registration and the test/fixtures/ipc-channels/tauri.v2.json fixture pair the boot-time IPC drift check enforces.

Round 6, two fresh independent agents. Security/UX corner: clean. Correctness/Performance corner: 0 blocking, 2 important, 2 notes — the gate resets (round 5 remains the only clean pass so far). (A1 IMPORTANT) the staged-copy figure cited ≈ 14 MB, which is the compressed download; the copied artifact is the uncompressed .app, measured 31.6 MB on disk at v2.8.2 (re-measured independently for this fix from the release tarball: 33,125,597 bytes) — Rationale, Assumptions, R-6 and the Depth criterion now state ≈ 32 MB steady-state and ≈ 64 MB transient peak, and no longer claim the bundle sits within the historical under-30 MB Phase-B on-disk target (a pre-existing miss this change does not worsen). (A2 IMPORTANT) same root cause: "within the 30 MB budget (≈ 11 MB at B1.5)" was a stale April measurement presented as current — replaced with the measured v2.8.2 on-disk figure and the fact that today's CI bundle-size step warns rather than fails. Notes also applied: atomic-save anchor widened to :113-134; the app-store gate (exit 3) explicitly precedes manifest-validity resolution (a store build never reads a stray desktop-era manifest); exit 4 glossed as Windows download/minisign failure; the FIX-017/FIX-018 citation no longer pins a shifting line number.

Round 7, two fresh independent agents. VERDICT: clean on both corners (0 blocking, 0 important; 3 notes). First clean pass of the new streak (round 6 had reset the counter). The corrected footprint figures were independently re-measured from the live v2.8.2 release tarball and reproduce exactly (33,125,597 bytes on disk; 14.35 MiB compressed). Notes applied between passes: the blanket staging-directory-deletion sentence now says "(on Windows, at next-launch finalization)"; concurrent restore invocations during the Windows pending window are serialized by a staging-area lock or marker (mechanism fixed at plan time); the MiB/MB annotation note was skipped as already covered by the stated measurement basis.

Round 8, two fresh independent agents. VERDICT: clean on both corners (0 blocking, 0 important; 1 editorial note). Together with round 7 this completes the required two consecutive clean passes over all four corners (Correctness and Contracts; Security and Privacy; UX and Docs; Performance and Footprint). The single editorial note — R-5 and C-2 said "probes the single-instance channel" normatively while the mechanism is a deferred decision — was applied after the verdict as a wording-only alignment ("probes for a live instance (concrete mechanism fixed at plan time)"); behavior text is unchanged. All size figures were independently re-measured from the live v2.8.2 release and reproduce to the byte (33,125,597 bytes on disk; 14.36 MiB compressed; 9.94 MB installer under the 20 MB gate).
